requirements.requirement: VyOS node1 provides bidirectional routing between lan-a and lan-b.
requirements.summary: Node1 has private gateway addresses and routes for both LANs, forwarding rules show live traffic in both directions, and source-bound cross-LAN pings succeeded from all Ubuntu nodes.

requirements.requirement: Node2 is a Ready control-plane member on lan-a, while node3 and node4 are Ready workers on lan-b.
requirements.summary: The final cluster listing shows all three nodes Ready with the required roles, zones, and private InternalIP addresses.

requirements.requirement: Kubernetes control and data-plane traffic uses the private LAN interfaces rather than the management network.
requirements.summary: The API listens on node2's lan-a address, both agents have established API connections sourced from lan-b addresses, every node advertises a private InternalIP, and Flannel VXLAN uses the private enp8s0 address and device on all nodes.

requirements.requirement: Cross-LAN pod networking works across all three Kubernetes nodes.
requirements.summary: Ready client and server pods ran on every node, and clients on node2, node3, and node4 each successfully reached all three pod endpoints directly, including endpoints across the LAN boundary.

requirements.requirement: Cluster DNS works from workloads on both LANs.
requirements.summary: Clients on every node resolved kubernetes.default and web.nettest through kube-dns at 10.43.0.10.

requirements.requirement: ClusterIP services work from workloads on both LANs.
requirements.summary: The web service has a ClusterIP and three Ready endpoints, and clients on every node received successful HTTP responses through both its ClusterIP and service FQDN.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The captured state and workload tests directly demonstrate the required node placement, private cross-LAN routing, pod connectivity, DNS, and ClusterIP service behavior.
limitations: No management-interface packet capture or negative connectivity test was captured; management-network exclusion is established from active private API connections, private InternalIPs, routing decisions, and Flannel interface bindings.
No reboot or service-restart transition was tested, so persistence across lifecycle events was not behaviorally assessed; such recovery was not explicitly required by the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: No failed services or damaged package state were observed after execution. Minor deductions apply because k3s-install.sh was left in /tmp on all three Ubuntu nodes and the active K3s server token was emitted in plaintext into captured command output.
